deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio belongs to Riemann's treatment of the minimal surface bounded by two regular polygons lying in parallel planes. The material appeared posthumously as 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', edited by Hattendorff (1867). The surface is mapped to an s-plane slit along [1,1/k] and [-1/k,-1]. Here η is the Gauss-map variable of the Weierstrass-type representation, and X = (h/2K)∫ds/√((1-s²)(1-k²s²)).

(a) End of the square case. Corners of one bounding square correspond to s=1/m and s=1/m' on both edges of the slit. The reversal points of the normal correspond to s=1, s=1/k, and a point s=1/n on both slit edges, where n is fixed by d log η/ds = 0. The ordering is 1 > m > n > m' > k.

(b) Equilateral triangles. The page writes η = c((1-ms)/(1+ms))^{2/3}((1-ks)/(1+ks))^{1/3}. The exponents 2/3 and 1/3 encode two corners at 1/m (one on each slit edge) and one corner at 1/k.

(c) Constant determination. Put s=±1:
- η0 = c((1-m)/(1+m))^{2/3}((1-k)/(1+k))^{1/3}.
- η0' = c((1+m)/(1-m))^{2/3}((1+k)/(1-k))^{1/3}.
- Hence η0η0' = c², so c = √(η0η0').
- Also √(η0/η0') = ((1-m)/(1+m))^{2/3}((1-k)/(1+k))^{1/3}.
- For congruent triangles η0η0' = 1 and c = 1.

(d) Combinatorics. Corners of one triangle: s=1/m on both edges and s=1/k, so k<m<1. Reversal points of the normal: s=1, and s=1/n on both edges, so k<n<m.

(e) Determining n. My filled-in step: d log η/ds = -(4m/3)/(1-m²s²) - (2k/3)/(1-k²s²) = 0. This gives 2m(1-k²s²) + k(1-m²s²) = 0, i.e. s² = (2m+k)/(km(m+2k)), so n² = km(m+2k)/(2m+k).
- n lies between k and m because n²-k² = k(m²-k²)/(2m+k) > 0 and m²-n² = 2m(m²-k²)/(2m+k) > 0 (my verification).

(f) Second condition. Require η³(1/n) = η0³:
((1-m)/(1+m))²(1-k)/(1+k) = ((n-m)/(n+m))²(n-k)/(n+k).

(g) Elimination of n (carried out on the next page; filled in here). Write F(x) = (x-m)²(x-k)/((x+m)²(x+k)).
- Expanding gives F(x) = (xP(x) - Q(x))/(xP(x) + Q(x)), with P = x²+2mk+m² and Q = (k+2m)x² + m²k.
- At x=1: P = 1+m²+2mk and Q = k(1+m²)+2m.
- At x=n (using the value of n²): P = 2m(m+k)(m+2k)/(2m+k) and Q = 2km(m+k).
- Then (nP/Q)² = m(m+2k)³/(k(2m+k)³).
- The equation F(1) = F(n) is equivalent to P(1)/Q(1) = nP(n)/Q(n).
- Squaring yields Riemann's next-page relation k((1+m²+2mk)/(k(1+m²)+2m))² = m((2k+m)/(k+2m))³.

(h) Footnote. The treatment extends to non-regular polygons. In particular the same η holds for two triangles whose centres lie on a common perpendicular to their planes, provided |ηη'| takes the same value at the reversal points of the normal. Congruent triangles are an example.
errors: No mathematical errors found: c=√(η0η0'), the ratio formula, the n² formula, k<n<m, and the second equation (which, combined with n², gives the next page's k–m relation) all check out.

Minor imprecision: the condition η³=η0³ at s=1/n is really a modulus/phase-matching condition. Since 1/n>1/m, the factor (1-ms)^{2/3} has a non-real branch there; cubing removes the branch ambiguity, so the stated equation is fine but the justification is implicit.

results.what: Gauss-map (η) of the minimal surface bounded by two equilateral triangles in parallel planes, as an algebraic function on a slit s-plane, with branch exponents 2/3, 1/3 encoding the corners
results.modern_name: Weierstrass–Enneper representation with Schwarz–Christoffel-type Gauss map for polygonal Plateau problems
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous 1867, ed. Hattendorff); Weierstrass, Schwarz for related polygonal problems

results.what: Determination of the accessory parameter n from d log η/ds=0: n² = km(m+2k)/(2m+k), with k<n<m
Second condition η³(1/n)=η0³ leading to the transcendental-free algebraic relation between k and m
results.modern_name: closing/period condition for Plateau problem with two polygonal boundaries

results.what: Footnote: extension to non-regular, coaxial triangles under a modulus condition on ηη'
results.modern_name: generalization of Riemann's two-polygon minimal surfaces

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material printed in Riemann's posthumous memoir on minimal surfaces (Hattendorff 1867, in the Werke). The computations are correct and already attributed to him; at most it shows drafting details.

checkable.asserts: s² = (2m+k)/(k m (m+2k)), i.e. n² = k m (m+2k)/(2m+k)
the k solving the next page's k–m relation (here for m=1/2) satisfies this page's equation with n² as given (numerically ≈0)

transcription_corrections: In the deleted phrase near 'Möglichkeit der Constantenbestimmung' the struck-through words are only partly legible; 'Constantenbestimmung' is a guess.
The second equation's right side is ((n-m)/(n+m))²·(n-k)/(n+k), as transcribed. The handwriting of the last fraction is cramped but consistent with this reading.
